name: Calendar pattern
claim: The hour of the week explains part of the PM10 risk class at each station.
rival: The calendar profile gives no skill over a constant rule per station. Or outdoor air explains the pattern (see H-08).
test: Train a calendar-only model on the training period. Compare it with the station base-rate baseline on the validation period.
refuted_if: The calendar-only model does not do better than the baseline on the primary metric for at least 3 of the 4 stations. Margin fixed in the pre-registration sheet.

name: Persistence
claim: Recent readings (last hours) add skill over the calendar for the next 1 to 24 hours.
rival: Recent readings add no skill over the calendar-only model.
test: Compare the short-term model with the calendar-only model on the validation period, for each horizon.
refuted_if: The short-term model does not do better than the calendar-only model for horizon 1 hour. Margin fixed in the pre-registration sheet.

name: Station effect
claim: The stations have different PM levels because of the stations, not because of the sensors.
rival: The level differences come from sensor type, calibration or position.
test: Look for co-located reference measurements in the Airparif reports. Compare sensor types per station (G-04).
refuted_if: A source shows a sensor bias of the same size as the difference between stations. If no source exists, the status stays OPEN and we say that we cannot test it.

name: Season
claim: The month or season changes the risk after the hour of the week is known.
rival: The month adds no information after the hour of the week.
test: Add month features to the calendar-only model. Compare on the validation period.
refuted_if: The model with month features does not do better than the model without them. Margin fixed in the pre-registration sheet.

name: Transfer
claim: A model trained on some stations gives useful predictions for a station that it did not see.
rival: Each station needs its own model.
test: Train without one station (leave one station out). Test on that station. Compare with a model trained on that station.
refuted_if: The transfer model does not do better than the station base-rate baseline on the left-out station.

name: Relevance
claim: PM levels in these stations are often above a health reference, so a warning has value.
rival: Levels are rarely above a health reference, so a warning has little value.
test: When G-14 is closed, count days with a daily mean above the reference, per station, on Silver data.
refuted_if: Fewer than one day per month on average is above the reference at all stations.

name: Missing data
claim: Missing values are linked to the PM level (for example outages near high levels).
rival: Missing values are not linked to the PM level.
test: Compare the PM10 distribution in the 24 hours before each outage with random 24-hour windows of the same station and month.
refuted_if: No difference with the test fixed in the pre-registration sheet.

name: Cause of weekly pattern
claim: Rail traffic causes the weekday and weekend difference.
rival: Ventilation schedule, outdoor road traffic, outdoor PM or sensor maintenance cause the difference.
test: When a traffic source is found (G-16), compare hourly trains with hourly PM10. Compare with outdoor PM (S-10).
refuted_if: PM10 does not follow train numbers when the calendar is fixed, or outdoor PM explains the same part.
